_comment: Errorful learning: each topic maps to a list of plausible-wrong reasoning chains. The 'wrong' field is what the user is asked to critique. Hand-curated for high-yield clinical scenarios.

Hyperkalemia.wrong: Give magnesium first to stabilize the cardiac membrane.
Hyperkalemia.why_wrong: Calcium (gluconate or chloride), not magnesium, stabilizes the cardiac membrane in hyperkalemia.
Hyperkalemia.right: Calcium gluconate 1 g IV stabilizes the membrane within minutes.

Sepsis.wrong: Hold antibiotics until blood cultures result, then narrow.
Sepsis.why_wrong: Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour of recognition save lives; cultures are drawn before antibiotics but you do NOT delay therapy waiting for them.
Sepsis.right: Draw cultures, give broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour, fluids 30 mL/kg, lactate.

Anaphylaxis.wrong: Give IV diphenhydramine first; epinephrine if no response.
Anaphylaxis.why_wrong: Epinephrine IM is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. H1 blockers and steroids are adjuncts, not primary therapy.
Anaphylaxis.right: Epinephrine 0.3-0.5 mg IM into the lateral thigh immediately.

ARDS.wrong: Use 10 mL/kg tidal volumes to maintain minute ventilation.
ARDS.why_wrong: Low tidal volume ventilation (6 mL/kg of predicted body weight) reduces mortality. High Vt causes volutrauma.
ARDS.right: 6 mL/kg PBW, plateau pressure <30, PEEP per ARDSnet table.

Aortic stenosis.wrong: Give phenylephrine for hypotension to raise SVR.
Aortic stenosis.why_wrong: Phenylephrine is actually correct in AS — increases afterload and coronary perfusion. (Trick: this is the right answer; what's WRONG is reflexively reaching for ephedrine or fluid bolus alone in AS hypotension.)
Aortic stenosis.right: Maintain afterload (phenylephrine), preload, sinus rhythm, normal HR.

Malignant hyperthermia.wrong: Stop the volatile, give cooling, and continue surgery.
Malignant hyperthermia.why_wrong: Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV is the definitive treatment and must be given immediately. Stopping volatile and cooling are necessary but not sufficient.
Malignant hyperthermia.right: Stop trigger, dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV, hyperventilate 100% O2, cool, treat hyperkalemia.

LAST.wrong: Bolus epinephrine 1 mg IV like ACLS.
LAST.why_wrong: In LAST, use SMALLER doses of epinephrine (≤1 mcg/kg) — the 1 mg ACLS dose can worsen arrhythmia. Lipid emulsion is the key.
LAST.right: Stop the local anesthetic, secure airway, intralipid 1.5 mL/kg bolus then 0.25 mL/kg/min infusion.

Succinylcholine.wrong: Sux is safe in burn patients within the first 24 hours.
Succinylcholine.why_wrong: Sux is contraindicated in burns >24-48 hours old due to upregulated extrajunctional ACh receptors causing massive K+ efflux. The first 24h window is debatable; safest to avoid.
Succinylcholine.right: Avoid sux in burns >24-48h, denervation injuries, prolonged immobility, MS, ALS, muscular dystrophies.

Hyponatremia.wrong: Correct rapidly with 3% saline regardless of chronicity.
Hyponatremia.why_wrong: Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia causes osmotic demyelination (ODS). Limit correction to ≤8-10 mEq/L in 24h.
Hyponatremia.right: Acute symptomatic: 3% saline 100 mL bolus. Chronic: ≤8-10 mEq/L per 24h, fluid restrict, treat cause.

Afib with RVR.why_wrong: Cardioversion is for HEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE afib. For stable RVR, rate control with beta blocker or diltiazem first; consider rhythm control after.
Afib with RVR.right: If unstable → cardiovert. If stable → rate control (metoprolol/diltiazem), anticoagulate per CHA2DS2-VASc.

STEMI.wrong: Tissue plasminogen activator is first-line if PCI is available within 90 minutes.
STEMI.why_wrong: PCI is the preferred reperfusion strategy when available within 90 min door-to-balloon. tPA is for when PCI is NOT available within 120 min.
STEMI.right: PCI within 90 min if available, otherwise tPA. Aspirin + heparin + dual antiplatelet.

DKA.wrong: Start insulin immediately — fluids can wait.
DKA.why_wrong: Volume resuscitation with normal saline comes FIRST. Insulin without fluids worsens intracellular potassium shifts. Also check K+ before insulin — replace if <3.3.
DKA.right: Fluids first (NS), check K+ (replace if low), then insulin drip. Add D5W when glucose <250.

GI bleed.why_wrong: Restrictive transfusion (target 7 g/dL) reduces mortality in upper GI bleed. Higher targets worsen rebleeding.
GI bleed.right: Restrictive: target 7 g/dL. PPI, octreotide if variceal, urgent endoscopy.

AKI.wrong: Start CRRT immediately for any AKI with creatinine >3.
AKI.why_wrong: RRT indications are AEIOU: Acidosis, Electrolyte disturbance (K+), Intoxications, Overload (refractory), Uremia. Creatinine number alone doesn't trigger.
AKI.right: RRT for refractory hyperkalemia, severe acidosis, fluid overload not responding, uremic complications, dialyzable toxins.

Hypotension after induction.wrong: Bolus 1L crystalloid first; if no response, start pressors.
Hypotension after induction.why_wrong: Most post-induction hypotension is from anesthetic-induced venodilation/myocardial depression, not hypovolemia. Phenylephrine or ephedrine is faster and more appropriate than fluid alone.
Hypotension after induction.right: Reduce volatile, bolus phenylephrine or ephedrine, consider fluid only if volume status warrants.

Bronchospasm.wrong: Switch to TIVA and stop inhalational agents.
Bronchospasm.why_wrong: Volatile agents are bronchodilators (sevo, iso, des). Going DEEPER on volatile is part of the treatment, not stopping it.
Bronchospasm.right: Deepen anesthesia, 100% O2, albuterol via ETT, epinephrine if severe, rule out anaphylaxis.

Difficult airway.wrong: Give succinylcholine and try direct laryngoscopy first.
Difficult airway.why_wrong: Anticipated difficult airway → AWAKE intubation (fiberoptic) preserves spontaneous ventilation. Paralyzing first risks 'cannot intubate, cannot ventilate'.
Difficult airway.right: Awake fiberoptic intubation with topicalization. Have backup (LMA, surgical airway) ready.

Pneumothorax tension.wrong: Get a chest X-ray to confirm before decompression.
Pneumothorax tension.why_wrong: Tension pneumothorax is a CLINICAL diagnosis (hypotension, tracheal deviation, absent breath sounds). Decompress immediately; don't wait for imaging.
Pneumothorax tension.right: Needle decompression in 2nd ICS midclavicular OR 4th-5th ICS midaxillary, then chest tube.

Stroke acute.wrong: Give aspirin immediately and tPA within 4.5 hours.
Stroke acute.why_wrong: Aspirin is HELD for 24h after tPA. Order: confirm ischemic (CT no bleed), tPA if window, then aspirin at 24h.
Stroke acute.right: Non-contrast CT first (rule out bleed), tPA <4.5h if eligible, no aspirin x 24h after tPA.

Status epilepticus.wrong: Load phenytoin 20 mg/kg as the first agent.
Status epilepticus.why_wrong: Benzodiazepines (lorazepam IV or IM midazolam) are FIRST-line. Phenytoin/levetiracetam are SECOND-line if seizures continue.
Status epilepticus.right: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (or IM midazolam if no IV), then levetiracetam or phenytoin if persists.

Code blue.wrong: High-quality compressions to a depth of 1 inch at 100/min.
Code blue.why_wrong: Compression depth should be 2-2.4 inches (5-6 cm) in adults. 1 inch is grossly insufficient.
Code blue.right: Compressions 2-2.4 inches, rate 100-120/min, allow full recoil, minimize interruptions.

Hypoxemia.wrong: Increase FiO2 to 100% and the SpO2 will correct in any cause.
Hypoxemia.why_wrong: Shunt physiology (e.g. severe pneumonia, ARDS) does NOT correct fully with O2 because blood bypasses ventilated alveoli entirely.
Hypoxemia.right: Differentiate FiO2 vs V/Q mismatch vs shunt vs diffusion vs hypoventilation. Shunt needs PEEP/recruitment, not just FiO2.

Vasopressor septic shock.wrong: Start dopamine first — it's the most balanced pressor.
Vasopressor septic shock.why_wrong: Norepinephrine is first-line in septic shock (lower arrhythmia rate vs dopamine, similar mortality benefit).
Vasopressor septic shock.right: Norepinephrine first, add vasopressin or epinephrine if MAP <65 despite norepi.

Massive transfusion.wrong: Give crystalloid until BP improves, then start blood products.
Massive transfusion.why_wrong: Massive hemorrhage = activate MTP early. Aggressive crystalloid worsens dilutional coagulopathy and hypothermia. 1:1:1 ratio of pRBC:FFP:platelets.
Massive transfusion.right: Activate MTP, 1:1:1 ratio, calcium replacement, keep warm, source control.

PE massive.wrong: Heparin alone is sufficient for any PE with hypotension.
PE massive.why_wrong: Massive PE (hemodynamic instability) → consider thrombolysis (tPA) or embolectomy. Heparin alone insufficient when patient is crashing.
PE massive.right: Stable PE → heparin. Massive PE with shock → tPA or surgical/catheter embolectomy.

ICU delirium.wrong: Start scheduled benzodiazepines for any agitation in the ICU.
ICU delirium.why_wrong: Benzos WORSEN delirium. Treat reversible causes; if pharmacologic needed, consider haloperidol or dexmedetomidine.
ICU delirium.right: Reverse causes (pain, sleep, sedation interruption), mobilize, minimize benzos, use dexmedetomidine if sedation needed.

Reversal neuromuscular blockade.wrong: Sugammadex works for all neuromuscular blockers.
Reversal neuromuscular blockade.why_wrong: Sugammadex specifically reverses aminosteroids (rocuronium, vecuronium). It does NOT reverse benzylisoquinolines (cisatracurium, atracurium).
Reversal neuromuscular blockade.right: Sugammadex for roc/vec. Neostigmine + glycopyrrolate for cisatracurium/atracurium.

Spinal high.wrong: Give vasopressors and hold fluids until BP improves.
Spinal high.why_wrong: High spinal causes hypotension AND respiratory failure (phrenic nerve involvement). AIRWAY is the priority — intubate, then vasopressors and fluids.
Spinal high.right: Airway/intubate first, IVF, vasopressors (ephedrine/phenylephrine), atropine for bradycardia, supportive care.

Local anesthetic max dose.wrong: Lidocaine max is 7 mg/kg with or without epinephrine.
Local anesthetic max dose.why_wrong: Lidocaine max is 4 mg/kg WITHOUT epi, 7 mg/kg WITH epi. Don't conflate the two.
Local anesthetic max dose.right: Lidocaine: 4 mg/kg plain, 7 mg/kg with epi. Bupivacaine: 2 mg/kg plain, 3 mg/kg with epi.

Aspiration.wrong: Lavage with saline through the ETT to clear aspirated material.
Aspiration.why_wrong: Saline lavage SPREADS aspirated material distally. Suction only — do not lavage.
Aspiration.right: Suction (no lavage), 100% O2, PEEP, bronchoscopy if particulate, supportive care. No prophylactic antibiotics or steroids.
